articles.title: Micah Parsons blames Jayden Daniels for clock mismanagement, says Commanders QB 'probably cost' Dan Quinn his job
articles.summary: Parsons didn't hold back on his Bleacher Report show, "The Edge with Micah Parsons."
articles.body:
Green Bay Packers sack artist Micah Parsons won't play Sunday night against his old team , the Dallas Cowboys, but he's nearing his return from the torn ACL that prematurely ended his first season with the Packers.

Despite his on-field absence, his voice is still being heard, including on his Bleacher Report show, "The Edge with Micah Parsons," where the five-time Pro Bowler blamed Jayden Daniels for the Washington Commanders' embarrassing clock mismanagement in the final moments of their 27-27 tie against the New York Giants over the weekend.

"Jayden Daniels probably cost my man Dan Quinn his job, to be honest with you," Parsons said on an episode that was clipped early Tuesday .

Quinn was Parsons' defensive coordinator for three seasons from 2021-23 in Dallas. During that span, Parsons became NFL Defensive Rookie of the Year and earned three All-Pro honors.

Parsons continued: "I'm a big Jayden Daniels fan, but, the reality is, he probably cost a lot of people their jobs this past weekend."

The Commanders (1-3-1) were gifted a chance at a Week 5 win in overtime once the Giants (3-1-1) turned the ball over. Washington recorded the takeaway on New York's second series of the extra frame. On the Giants' first, kicker Dominic Zvada missed a potential go-ahead 46-yard field goal.

Then New York running back Cam Skattebo fumbled an opportunity for Zvada to try one more kick, which could have been a game-winner. Washington, which led 27-13 early in the fourth quarter, quickly reached field-goal range. Instead of spiking the ball to set up a game-winning field-goal attempt, the Commanders opted for one final play before that possible kick.

Daniels dubiously took a sack and stayed on the ground for a few seconds before seemingly remembering the gravity of the situation. Washington had no timeouts, and the clock was ticking. Most of the starting offense didn't appear to have a sense of urgency.

Ultimately, Daniels and Co. scurried to spike the ball, but they couldn't get lined up in time to do so, and the game unceremoniously concluded with the score tied.

"All respectfully, we get coached so much on these situations that I'm a defensive player and this is programmed to me," Parsons said. "I know what to do in those situations." Parsons went on: "There's no way I'm taking a sack with 14 seconds left and no timeouts. And, mind you, it'd be different if Jayden Daniels was a rookie. This is your third year. You've been to the NFC championship game, you've been in big moments before. To me, even after the sack, you're casually getting up. ... I'm like, 'You just took a sack ...' He's not even urgently getting up. "… If people want to say QBs win or lose games, and, as you can see, they just won or lost the game on the QB's hands, this is your job, bro. ... This is your job to be prepared, to understand the game and understand situations. That's in your job profile. And you're telling me, 'Oh, we're going to pay this guy eventually $60 million?' This cannot happen."

"All respectfully, we get coached so much on these situations that I'm a defensive player and this is programmed to me," Parsons said. "I know what to do in those situations."

Parsons went on: "There's no way I'm taking a sack with 14 seconds left and no timeouts. And, mind you, it'd be different if Jayden Daniels was a rookie. This is your third year. You've been to the NFC championship game, you've been in big moments before. To me, even after the sack, you're casually getting up. ... I'm like, 'You just took a sack ...' He's not even urgently getting up.

"… If people want to say QBs win or lose games, and, as you can see, they just won or lost the game on the QB's hands, this is your job, bro. ... This is your job to be prepared, to understand the game and understand situations. That's in your job profile. And you're telling me, 'Oh, we're going to pay this guy eventually $60 million?' This cannot happen."

Daniels was playing in his third game of the season and his first since dislocating his left elbow again . That injury took place in Week 2 at Dallas.

The 2024 NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year dazzled at times during his return, particularly with his legs. Wearing a brace on the elbow of his non-throwing arm, he ran for 103 yards and a pair of scores. Plus, the former No. 2 overall pick completed 17 of 25 passes for 199 yards.

His talent remains tantalizing. But more than a season has passed since he piloted Washington to its first NFC title game in 33 years. His durability has been questioned, and, on Sunday, his leadership was put under a magnifying glass .

Quinn took responsibility and admitted that the right call would have been to simply stop the clock with a spike or a throwaway out of bounds . They didn't need to gain more yards; they could have attempted a potential game-winning field goal earlier, Quinn said.

He also told reporters that the end-of-game sequencing "does not fall on" Daniels, who didn't get into specifics about what went down in that fateful situation. In the locker room, Commanders left guard Chris Paul said via 7News DC's Scott Abraham that Washington not having any timeouts left was discussed in the huddle before the final snap, but other players gave less convincing answers when asked about the matter .

"We've got to stop the clock," Daniels said postgame. "We've got to know the situation. We've got to relay that as an offense. It starts with everybody, top down. Ultimately, it's on me."

Some fans wanted more from Daniels at the mic, and so did Parsons.

"I would like to see more accountability myself," he said. "And I'm a player. I'm a big JD5 fan, but that's inexcusable, bro. The lack of urgency, that's something ... I would've had to say something in the locker room. I would've had to come talk to him, like, 'Yo, that's not OK.'"

Parsons emphasized that situations like the one Daniels ostensibly spaced on are drilled home repeatedly during an NFL season.

"Every day," he said. "Like on Wednesday, we bring up end of half four-minute drill. We talk about it. Thursdays, we literally do two-minute situations. We change the clock, change the time, change the point differential. They need a score, gotta-have-it situation, whatever — we do those situations every week. "On Fridays, red-zone situations, we talk about it. What's the mindset? ... We go through all these situations every week, so there's no way that you don't know these situations. We even go through mock games where we walk through these situations. So, to me, this is a lack of preparation, a lack of mentality and a lack of urgency by the man on campus. That just can't happen."

We change the clock, change the time, change the point differential. They need a score, gotta-have-it situation, whatever — we do those situations every week.

"On Fridays, red-zone situations, we talk about it. What's the mindset? ... We go through all these situations every week, so there's no way that you don't know these situations. We even go through mock games where we walk through these situations. So, to me, this is a lack of preparation, a lack of mentality and a lack of urgency by the man on campus. That just can't happen."

While Quinn was at the helm for the Commanders' storybook run to the NFC championship just two seasons ago, he's now 18-20-1 during his stay in Washington. Since a 3-2 start last season, Quinn's Commanders are 3-13-1.

articles.title: Recently unsealed report on coach Brian Flores contains 'racial stereotypes,' according to lawyers
articles.summary: A recently unsealed recruiting firm's report on Brian Flores has multiple examples of “racial stereotypes” and amounts to unlawful retaliation for the coach'...
articles.body:
A recently unsealed recruiting firm's report on Brian Flores has multiple examples of "racial stereotypes" and amounts to unlawful retaliation for the coach's discrimination lawsuit against the NFL, according to his lawyers.

The Korn Ferry report that was made public Tuesday — a copy of which was obtained by The Associated Press — contains a list of six strengths and seven weaknesses which Flores' attorneys say show the league still uses racial stereotypes in hiring and is unlawfully retaliating against the coach for his lawsuit against the league alleging racial discrimination.

The report, which was first published by Front Office Sports , was prepared in connection with the Las Vegas Raiders' coaching vacancy in 2024. Flores is now the defensive coordinator for the Minnesota Vikings.

"The recently unsealed documents demonstrate two unfortunate, but unsurprising, realities," attorney Michael J. Willemin wrote in a statement. "First, that Mr. Flores' decision to hold the league and its teams accountable for systemic race discrimination has been met with unlawful retaliation. Second, discrimination continues to play a significant role in the hiring process for NFL Head Coaches, as evidenced by the fact that the candidate profile prepared for the Raiders leans heavily on racial stereotypes. We and Mr. Flores are committed to eradicating the institutional racism and retaliation that permeates the league, its teams and their partners."

The NFL didn't immediately respond to a request for comment.

One of the strengths listed says Flores is a "polished and a good presenter despite growing up in Brownsville, Brooklyn (same as Mike Tyson). He was able to build a strong friendship with a billionaire's son which gave him opportunities to socialize and learn how to build relationships with white-collar and upper-class individuals."

Brownsville is a predominately Black and Hispanic neighborhood in Brooklyn.

One of the negatives says Flores "can fool you with his polish upwards. Has little people skills, lacks self-awareness and can sometimes exhibit erratic behavior. (Former Dolphins quarterback Tua Tagovailoa's) statements have opened the narrative that Brian was "pessimistic and adversarial" and his style "shattered his confidence."

Other negatives listed included that Flores' "personality is unpredictable" and that he "once threatened violence to his GM and made irrational demands during an ownership meeting."

The report goes on to say that a long-term senior executive said Flores "may have changed since, but he was the worst hiring decision we've ever made."

The final negative was that the ongoing litigation related to the coach's discrimination case against the NFL could cause a distraction.

Flores, who is Black, sued the league and three teams in February 2022, alleging the league was "rife with racism" regarding its hiring practices when it comes to Black coaches. Flores had recently been fired from his head coaching job with the Miami Dolphins.

He was later joined in the lawsuit by fellow Black coaches Steve Wilks and Ray Horton.

articles.title: NFL suspends Rams LT Alaric Jackson 2 games for punching Bradley Chubb in the face after 'Monday Night Football'
articles.summary: The incident took place on the field after Buffalo's 37-34 overtime win at Sofi Stadium in Los Angeles.
articles.body:
The NFL has suspended Los Angeles Rams left tackle Alaric Jackson for two games after he punched Bills linebacker Bradley Chubb in the face in the aftermath of "Monday Night Football."

In its announcement Tuesday, the league stated that Jackson was in violation of Rule 12, Section 3, Article 1 regarding "any act which is contrary to the generally understood principles of sportsmanship."

The incident took place on the field after Buffalo's 37-34 overtime win at SoFi Stadium in Los Angeles on Monday. Jackson was exchanging his jersey with a Bills player when Chubb said something to Jackson and pointed at him from a distance.

Chubb turned around and walked away after his comment. Jackson followed Chubb, and the two exchanged words. Jackson then punched Chubb in the face. Chubb's teammates pulled him away from the scene before the incident could escalate further.

ESPN cameras recorded the incident during its postgame coverage.

It's not clear what Chubb or Jackson said leading up to the punch. Jackson had not addressed the incident as of Tuesday. Chubb said this of the incident to the California Post Monday night.

"It was a close game," Chubb said, per the Post. "And, you know, they always catch the second guy, so I let him swing and my teammates held me back and I just chilled."

Tough time for Rams to be without Jackson

The suspension of Jackson leaves the Rams without a key player during a critical juncture of their season.

A Rams team that entered the season as the favorite to win the Super Bowl fell to 2-3 with the loss and will now play its next two games without its most important offensive lineman.

Backup David Quessenberry will replace Jackson at left tackle while Jackson is out, protecting Matthew Stafford's blindside. Head coach Sean McVay confirmed Quessenberry's promotion Tuesday night.

Jackson will miss upcoming against the Arizona Cardinals and Las Vegas Raiders.

Against the Raiders, the Rams will be up against five-time Pro Bowl pass rusher Maxx Crosby. Against the Cardinals, they'll face former Pro Bowler Josh Sweat, who tallied a career-high 12 sacks last season.

After facing the Raiders, the Rams will play the Chargers, Commanders and Cardinals again before a Week 11 bye. They'll need a strong showing in that five-game stretch to remain afloat in the NFC playoff picture.

The official suspension statement read, in part: "After the game, as players were shaking hands and exchanging jerseys, Jackson struck Buffalo linebacker Bradley Chubb in the face after a brief confrontation, violating Rule 12, Section 3, Article 1, which applies to "any act which is contrary to the generally understood principles of sportsmanship." articles.title: Rams sign CB Damarion Williams to practice squad, cut LB Jamie Sheriff
articles.summary: The Rams added a secondary piece to their practice squad who's bounced around the league for a few years.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams made a pair of practice squad moves, according to the NFL transaction wire, signing cornerback Damarion Williams and releasing linebacker Jamie Sheriff .

Williams, 28, is a 5-foot-10, 183-pound corner who finished his college career at Houston. The Baltimore Ravens selected him in the fourth round (141st overall) of the 2022 NFL Draft. Williams appeared in 14 games as a rookie, totaling 24 tackles (15 solo), one tackle for loss and two pass breakups. He played in one game in 2023. In 15 career games, he has yet to start and has no interceptions or sacks.

Williams has bounced around since the Ravens drafted him in the fourth round in 2022. Baltimore waived him in August 2024, and he later landed with the Seahawks and Buccaneers, spending time on both practice squads. Tampa Bay waived him Aug. 30 and then from injured reserve Sept. 3, making the Rams his fourth organization.

Sheriff, 26, is a 6-foot-1, 254-pound linebacker who played at Mississippi Gulf Coast and South Alabama. Sheriff has appeared in three NFL games: two in 2024, one with Carolina and one with Seattle, and one with the Seahawks in 2025. He has one career tackle, which came in 2025, and is a one-time Super Bowl champion.

Sheriff went undrafted in 2024 and signed with Seattle, was claimed by Carolina the day after Seattle waived him, and played 17 snaps in the Panthers' Week 1 loss. He returned to the Seahawks' practice squad that September and stayed with Seattle until he was waived Aug. 30, making the Rams his third team.

Both moves are practice squad transactions and do not affect the Rams' 53-man roster.

articles.title: Chargers sign former Bengals backup as Justin Herbert insurance
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Chargers are 0-5 going into Week 6 after suffering a 23-17 loss in Week 5 to the Denver Broncos. Things are just not clicking for quarterback...
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Chargers are 0-5 going into Week 6 after suffering a 23-17 loss in Week 5 to the Denver Broncos. Things are just not clicking for quarterback Justin Herbert , as the offense has been putrid so far. On Tuesday, the organization found a new insurance plan behind Herbert by signing a former backup from the Cincinnati Bengals.

Reports indicate that the Chargers are officially signing Jake Browning , according to NFL insider Tom Pelissero. It is currently unknown if Browning is signing with the active roster or practice squad, as that information will be revealed in due time.

"The Chargers are signing veteran QB Jake Browning, per source," Pelissero reported.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Browning has appeared in 17 career games for the Bengals throughout his career, starting in 10 games. He stepped in for five contests last season while Joe Burrow was dealing with a turf toe injury that sidelined him for several weeks. The 30-year-old signal-caller joins the Chargers with 2,702 passing yards, 18 touchdowns, and 15 interceptions accumulated throughout his career, while owning a 68.5% completion percentage.

Jake Browning has not appeared in a single game yet in the 2026-27 campaign. Ideally, that remains the case now that he is in Los Angeles, as sticking with Justin Herbert is the ideal scenario for the Chargers. Even with the 28-year-old struggling so much this season.

Herbert is on pace for the worst year of his career. Through five games, he's only thrown for 937 yards and five touchdowns while leading the league with seven interceptions. His 59.4% completion percentage is by far the lowest it's ever been since he entered the NFL in 2020.

The two-time Pro Bowler will have a chance to get back on track in Week 6. However, that may be a difficult task, as the Chargers are set to take on Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs on the road in their next game.

articles.title: Former 49ers practice squad member signed by Jets
articles.summary: Quinton Bell spent the 2026 offseason with the 49ers after bouncing around the league since 2019.
articles.body:
A recent member of the San Francisco 49ers practice squad is headed elsewhere. The New York Jets signed defensive end Quinton Bell this week to their practice squad after the 49ers released Bell on Aug. 30.

The 6-foot-4 and 258-pound Bell recorded four tackles and one special teams stop in preseason action this summer.

The 49ers were the latest stop in a career that has taken Bell across the league after he signed a one-year deal on July 29, 2026. He has appeared in 33 games with three starts over four seasons with Tampa Bay (2020), Atlanta (2022) and Miami (2024-25). In that time, he has totaled 38 tackles (18 solo), one sack, one pass breakup and one forced fumble.

The Las Vegas Raiders selected Bell in the seventh round (No. 230 overall) of the 2019 NFL Draft. Counting the Raiders, the Jets are his sixth organization.

A Long Beach, Calif., native, Bell was a high school track star at Costa Mesa High School. He switched from receiver to defensive end as a senior at Prairie View A&M and earned second-team all-SWAC honors. He became the first Prairie View player drafted since 1980.

articles.title: NFL has been "monitoring developments" in Tyreek Hill case
articles.summary: On Tuesday, a jury entered a mixed verdict in the civil lawsuit filed against free-agent receiver Tyreek Hill by his former wife, Keeta Vaccaro.
articles.body:
On Tuesday, a jury entered a mixed verdict in the civil lawsuit filed against free-agent receiver Tyreek Hill by his former wife, Keeta Vaccaro. The verdict comes at a time when the NFL is investigating Hill for the allegations Vaccaro has made.

"We have been monitoring developments in the matter which remains under review of the personal conduct policy," an NFL spokesperson told PFT on Tuesday night, after the verdict was returned.

The civil verdict is not binding on the league, as to either the counts on which he lost or the counts on which he won. The NFL's investigation is independent of that process.

The key question is whether Vaccaro will cooperate with the NFL. It has no power to issue subpoenas; if, for example, the verdict leads to a prompt settlement, a confidentiality provision could prevent her from talking to NFL investigators.

Regardless, the verdict becomes evidence that the NFL could utilize, along with the transcript of Vaccaro's sworn testimony. It's unclear when the NFL's investigation will conclude, or whether the civil verdict would prompt the league to place Hill on paid leave as the investigation proceeds.
